presentingComplaint: Sudden onset of a widespread pinpoint rash, gum bleeding and easy bruising over 3 days, with a mild non-throbbing headache today that prompted her to attend.
history: Previously healthy 34-year-old woman, non-pregnant, with a viral upper respiratory illness about 2 weeks ago that has resolved. Over the last 3 days she noticed a non-blanching pinpoint rash spreading up both shins, then thighs and forearms, spontaneous gum bleeding when brushing teeth, one episode of self-limiting epistaxis, and menorrhagia with her current period. Today she developed a dull global headache and, because a friend told her low platelets with headache can be a 'blood emergency', she attended. No confusion, no visual disturbance, no focal weakness, no fever, no diarrhoea, no recent new drugs (specifically no quinine, heparin, sulfonamides, or NSAIDs), no herbal or quinine-containing tonics, no alcohol excess. No prior bleeding history, normal menstrual and dental-extraction history. No joint pains, oral ulcers, photosensitivity or Raynaud phenomenon. No family history of bleeding or thrombosis. The overlapping concern at triage was thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (headache + thrombocytopenia), which must be actively excluded.
examination: Alert, fully oriented, comfortable. Scattered petechiae over both lower limbs, forearms and buccal mucosa, with a few ecchymoses over the shins. Wet purpura noted on the palate. No pallor, no jaundice, no lymphadenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly. No sternal tenderness. Neurological examination entirely normal (no confusion, no focal deficit, fundi normal). No signs of active large-vessel bleeding; abdomen soft and non-tender.

labs.peripheralSmear: Isolated thrombocytopenia; occasional large platelets; NO schistocytes, NO blasts, no leucoerythroblastic picture

imaging: Non-contrast CT head (performed to exclude intracranial bleed given headache + severe thrombocytopenia): no haemorrhage, no mass, normal.
microbiology: Not applicable (non-infective). H. pylori and HIV/HCV/HBV screening sent per ITP work-up; HIV/HCV/HBV negative.
differentialDiagnoses: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) - excluded by absence of microangiopathic haemolysis (normal Hb, no schistocytes, normal LDH/bilirubin, normal reticulocytes, normal renal function)
Disseminated intravascular coagulation - excluded by normal INR/aPTT/fibrinogen
Acute leukaemia / marrow infiltration - against: isolated thrombocytopenia with normal Hb and WBC, no blasts, no organomegaly
Drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia - no culprit drug exposure
Secondary ITP (SLE, HIV, HCV) - screening negative
finalDiagnosis: Primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) - isolated severe thrombocytopenia with mucocutaneous bleeding, a diagnosis of exclusion, with TTP and DIC actively ruled out.
citations: American Society of Hematology (ASH) - Immune Thrombocytopenia Guidelines - 2019
International Working Group - Standardization of Terminology and Diagnostic Criteria for ITP - 2009
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e - Disorders of Platelets and the Vessel Wall (Thrombocytopenia) - 2022
stewardship: Not applicable - non-infective condition; no antibiotics indicated. Management is immunomodulatory (corticosteroids +/- IVIG), not antimicrobial.
contraindications: Avoid platelet transfusion unless life-threatening haemorrhage (rapidly consumed; reserve for critical bleeding)
Avoid IM injections and invasive procedures until platelet count recovers
If TTP were suspected, platelet transfusion would be contraindicated - reinforces the need to exclude MAHA first
edgeCases: Headache with severe thrombocytopenia can falsely trigger a TTP pathway; the pentad is incomplete and MAHA markers are normal here
Intracranial haemorrhage is the feared complication at platelet <10 - CT head was appropriately normal
Menorrhagia may mask ongoing blood loss; monitor Hb serially
Rule out pseudothrombocytopenia (EDTA clumping) by repeating count in citrate tube if smear ambiguous
expectedMaiK: Isolated severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 8) with mucocutaneous/wet purpura, normal haemoglobin and white count, NO schistocytes, normal LDH/coagulation/renal function - points to ITP, not TTP or DIC.
